units.text: Recommendation ITU-T Y.3553 (09/2024): Cloud computing – Distributed cloud functional architecture

The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) is the United Nations specialized agency in the field of telecommunications, and information and communication technologies (ICTs). The ITU Telecommunication Standardization Sector (ITU-T) is a permanent organ of ITU. ITU-T is responsible for studying technical, operating and tariff questions and issuing Recommendations on them with a view to standardizing telecommunications on a worldwide basis. The World Telecommunication Standardization Assembly (WTSA), which meets every four years, establishes the topics for study by the ITU-T study groups which, in turn, produce Recommendations on these topics. The approval of ITU-T Recommendations is covered by the procedure laid down in WTSA Resolution 1. In some areas of information technology which fall within ITU-T's purview, the necessary standards are prepared on a collaborative basis with ISO and IEC. NOTE In this Recommendation, the expression "Administration" is used for conciseness to indicate both a telecommunication administration and a recognized operating agency. Compliance with this Recommendation is voluntary. However, the Recommendation may contain certain mandatory provisions (to ensure, e.g., interoperability or applicability) and compliance with the Recommendation is achieved when all of these mandatory provisions are met. The words "shall" or some other obligatory language such as "must" and the negative equivalents are used to express requirements. The use of such words does not suggest that compliance with the Recommendation is required of any party.

ITU draws attention to the possibility that the practice or implementation of this Recommendation may involve the use of a claimed Intellectual Property Right. This Recommendation specifies the functional architecture for the distributed cloud. It defines the following subjects: – Functions for distributed cloud; – Functional architecture for distributed cloud including reference points. Additionally, it describes relationship between cloud types and function groups for distributed cloud.

The following ITU-T Recommendations and other references contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this Recommendation. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All Recommendations and other references are subject to revision; users of this Recommendation are therefore encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent edition of the Recommendations and other references listed below. A list of the currently valid ITU-T Recommendations is regularly published. The reference to a document within this Recommendation does not give it, as a stand-alone document, the status of a Recommendation.
[ITU-T Y.3502] Recommendation ITU-T Y.3502 (2014), Information technology – Cloud computing – Reference architecture.
[ITU-T Y.3508] Recommendation ITU-T Y.3508 (2019), Cloud computing – Overview and high-level requirements of distributed cloud.
[ITU-T Y.3526] Recommendation ITU-T Y.3526 (2021), Cloud computing – Functional requirements of edge cloud management.
[ITU-T Y.3538] Recommendation ITU-T Y.3538 (2022), Cloud computing – Global management framework of distributed cloud.
This Recommendation uses the following terms defined elsewhere:
A cloud computing, which manages resource pools including resources in the edge of the network and enables cloud service. NOTE – Enabled cloud service on the core cloud is provided by CSP.

Distribution of cloud capabilities types to the edge of the network for enabling cloud services with low latency and real time processing on limited bandwidth by interworking among pools of physical or virtual resources.

A cloud computing deployed to the edge of the network accessed by cloud service customers (CSCs) with small capacity resources enabling cloud service. NOTE 1 – Enabled cloud service on the edge cloud is lightweight cloud service provided by a cloud service provider (CSP) depending on cloud service category. NOTE 2 – Lightweight cloud service refers to a portion of cloud service to reconfigure the functionality of cloud service to fit on edge cloud such as base station and gateway with small capacity resource.

The efficient and effective way to provide management of resources, data, services, applications, operation and maintenance and risks of edge cloud. NOTE 1 – The scope of edge cloud management is within an edge cloud. Each edge cloud has one edge cloud management. NOTE 2 – Edge cloud management coordinates with global management and other edge cloud managements.

Resource pool with limited computing, storage, network and other software and tools within one edge cloud. NOTE 1 – Each edge node belongs to only one edge cloud. Each edge cloud has at least one edge node. NOTE 2 – Edge node uses edge cloud management to expose its abilities and achieve coordination with other edge nodes.

A cloud computing hosted from core cloud to particular geographical regions. NOTE – Enabled cloud service on the regional cloud is entire or partial cloud service of core cloud provided by a cloud service provider (CSP).
This Recommendation uses the following abbreviations and acronyms:
ECM-FG Edge Cloud Management Function Group
OMM-F Operation and Maintenance Management Function
RBR-F Remote Backup and Recovery Function
RMS-F Resource Monitoring and Scheduling Function
SAM-F Service Awareness and Management Function
6 Relationship between cloud types and function groups for distributed cloud

This Recommendation realizes high-level functional requirements in [ITU-T Y.3508], and functional requirements in [ITU-T Y.3526] and [ITU-T Y.3538] (see Appendix I). The general functionalities related to cloud computing refer to CCRA in [ITU-T Y.3502], and specific functionalities are extended in this Recommendation (see Appendix II). Distributed cloud includes core cloud (CC), regional cloud (RC) and edge cloud (EC) as defined in [ITU-T Y.3508]. The global management (GM) in [ITU-T Y.3538] provides management capabilities for distributed cloud resources and cloud service distribution, with interacting among CC, RC and EC in the distributed cloud. The edge cloud management (ECM) defined in [ITU-T Y.3526] provides management for resources, data, services, applications, operation and maintenance and risks in EC, and cooperates with GM to achieve hierarchical and automatic management in distributed cloud. To support the three types of cloud (CC, RC and EC in distributed cloud) from the view of deployment, this Recommendation specifies six function groups from the view of logical functionalities, including connection management, service orchestration, service capabilities, resource abstraction and control, GM and ECM. Four of them are deployed in CC/RC, and three of them are deployed in EC as shown in Table 6-1. Specifically, functions in service capabilities function group are deployed in CC/RC and EC separately. RC has the same function groups with CC according to distributed cloud configuration models described in [ITU-T Y.3508].
Table 6-1 – Relationship between cloud types and function groups in distributed cloud

Cloud types in distributed Function groups in this Recommendation cloud Connection management function group (see clause 7.1) Service orchestration function group (see clause 7.2) CC/RC Service capabilities function group (see clause 7.3) Global management function group (see clause 7.5) Service capabilities function group (see clause 7.3) EC Resource abstraction and control function group (see clause 7.4) Edge cloud management function group (see clause 7.6)
Figure 7-1 shows the function groups and corresponding functions for distributed cloud.
Figure 7-1 – Function groups and functions for distributed cloud
The connection management function group in CC/RC includes network awareness function.

The network awareness function supports the following: – Providing on-demand network traffic control to mitigate congested network links; – Reallocating routing paths and allocating bandwidth; – Supporting routing for provisioned cloud service to CSCs; – Delivering cloud service requests to the best location by inspecting context information; NOTE – Context information includes cloud service context information and network service context information. Examples of cloud service context information are capacity of cloud, resource usage, service ID/name, service location and status of neighbour. Examples of network service context information are latency, bandwidth, quality of service (QoS), routing path, refer to [ITU-T Y.3508]; – Supporting network virtualization for dynamic network deployment.
The service orchestration function group in CC/RC includes service migration function.

The service migration function supports the following: – Migrating cloud services from one of distributed cloud resources to another one according to the configuration policy; NOTE 1 – The resources of distributed cloud are geographically distributed in CC, RC and EC. Service migration takes place among these resources. NOTE 2 – The configuration policy has the procedures of reverting and contingency plan for migration; – Taking a snapshot by the type of full snapshot or incremental snapshot; NOTE 3 – Full snapshot captures the entire content of the storage volume or VM for complete backup; NOTE 4 – Incremental snapshot captures the changes made from the last snapshot, to save storage space and reduce the time required for subsequent snapshot; – Relocating the cloud services dynamically to optimize performance and maintain service continuity.
The service capabilities function group is deployed in CC/RC and EC including service provisioning function and data processing function.
The service provisioning function which is deployed in CC/RC supports the following: – Enabling network access to the resource pool; – Self-service provisioning and administration on-demand.

The data processing function which is deployed in EC supports the following: – Pre-processing massive data of end device; NOTE – Pre-processing includes filtering, cleaning and optimizing the data; – Delivering the pre-processed data to the CC/RC.
7.4 Resource abstraction and control function group
The resource abstraction and control function group in EC includes end-device access control.

The end-device access control function supports the following: – Providing connectivity and access management of appropriate networks; – Restricting the availability of network resources to end devices; NOTE 1 – Availability of network includes the bandwidth limitation, network connection quality, etc.; – Supporting and managing network protocols to end device; – Complying with vulnerability assessment with security policies; NOTE 2 – Security policies include enforcement policies, system authentication policies, etc.; – Providing endpoint security protection with security software and firewall.

The GM function group in CC/RC includes six functions, which are operation and maintenance management, automatic management, service monitoring management, application deployment management, service risk management and resource allocation management.

The operation and maintenance management function supports the following: – Managing capabilities of the operation and maintenance of the distributed cloud; NOTE – Managing capabilities includes scheduling, deployment, allocation and monitoring of resources, etc.; – Providing global scheduling for running applications in distributed cloud; – Providing the management for policies of global scheduling.

The automatic management function supports the following: – Providing unified management capabilities which includes automatic provisioning, configuration and updating, as well as monitoring for cloud infrastructure; – Delivering cloud services continuously to the moving CSCs; – Providing automatic set-up of cloud infrastructure, including hardware initiation, network configuration and software installation; – Providing the capabilities to deploy cloud services efficiently in different locations; – Maintaining and upgrading cloud services automatically based on SLAs; – Recovering network connection from failures.

The service monitoring management function supports the following: – Providing the configuration for cloud service deployment; – Providing the cloud service monitoring during operation; – Providing the cloud service templates for CSCs to design and develop their applications; – Managing the interfaces of cloud services and network according to CSC's requirements.

The application deployment management function supports the following: – Supporting the deployment environment required by application; – Managing connection information among applications, refer to [ITU-T Y.3538]; NOTE – The connection information between distributed cloud includes connection topology and device connection information (e.g., PCIe, NVLink, etc.) between distributed cloud; – Managing interfaces for application monitoring; – Providing load balancing to deploy the application at the various types of platforms in the distributed cloud, (e.g., virtual machine-based platform, container-based platform, FaaS platform, etc.), refer to [ITU-T Y.3538].

The service risk management function supports the following: – Providing the capabilities to create and manage replicas and backups; – Providing the backup connections in case of network failure; – Managing the recovery process of cloud services in case of failure happened in CC/RC.

The resource allocation management function supports the following: – Allocating resources according to the best resource affinity and I/O congestion, refer to [ITU-T Y.3538]. NOTE 1 – The resource affinity means the distance between resources which is calculated through hop based on the connection information between corresponding devices and nodes. NOTE 2 – A hop is a path located between a source and a destination in distributed cloud. NOTE 3 – The resources are allocated according to the best resources' affinity (minimum distance between resources). NOTE 4 – The I/O congestion is calculated as the average value of how much is used against the maximum bandwidth by measuring the bandwidth of I/O devices (network and storage, etc.) during a specific time slot.

The edge cloud management function group in EC includes eight functions, which are remote software management, resource monitoring and scheduling, service awareness and management, offloading management, remote backup and recovery, location information maintenance, delay sensitive deployment, network service management.
The remote software management function supports the following: – Managing software with packages on edge node remotely; – Upgrading and rolling back software version.

The resource monitoring and scheduling function supports the following: – Monitoring and tracking the status and performance of resources, and enabling proactive resolution for identified issues (e.g., warning, fault, etc.); – Detecting resource changes automatically when resources are added or removed; – Scheduling appropriate resources from the resource pool to the cloud service; – Composing the resources according to the CSC's demand.

The service awareness and management function supports the following: – Supporting cloud service image repository; – Monitoring the status and progress of cloud service image when transmitted to the edge node; – Resuming cloud service image transmission at break-point; – Detecting the newly added cloud services; – Scheduling cloud services in a unified manner; – Gathering real-time monitoring information to check the status of cloud services.

The offloading management function supports the following: – Offloading the application based on context information from CC, RC, or neighbour EC to meet SLA; – Dividing cloud service to multiple tasks and offloading them to multiple edge nodes based on the predefined policy; – Integrating tasks of offloaded services based on context information.

The remote backup and recovery function supports the following: – Setting and triggering policies for backup and recovery based on CSC's demand; – Providing remote backup process to optimal resources in CC/RC; – Recovering data and services in resource-sufficient edge nodes.

The location information maintenance function supports the following: – Maintaining location and access information of cloud service to provide endpoint to the CSC. NOTE – Access information includes IP address, port number and authentication information.
The delay sensitive deployment function supports the following: – Deploying latency sensitive cloud service based on scheduling strategy to meet SLA.

The network service management function supports the following: – Establishing network connectivity for managing resources and providing cloud service efficiently; – Deploying virtual network functions to the EC; – Monitoring network service to support reliable network bandwidth and latency; – Detecting network service failures in the EC and recovering the connectivity.
Figure 8-1 shows the functional architecture for distributed cloud.
Figure 8-1 – Functional architecture for distributed cloud

The CC/RC comprises four function groups. The connection management function group (CM-FG), the service capabilities function group (SC-FG) and the service orchestration function group (SO-FG) interact with the global management function group (GM-FG). The EC comprises three function groups. The service capabilities function group (SC-FG), and resource abstraction and control function group (RAC-FG) interact with edge cloud management function group (ECM-FG). The GM-FG comprises six functions, which are the operation and maintenance management function (OMM-F), the monitoring and management function (SMM-F), service risk management function (SRM-F), the automatic management function (AM-F), the application deployment management function (ADM-F) and the resource allocation management function (RAM-F). These functions interact with CM-FG, SC-FG and SO-FG and ECM-FG. The ECM-FG comprises eight functions, which are the remote software management (RSM-F), which are the resource monitoring and scheduling (RMS-F), the service awareness and management (SAM-F), the offloading management (OM-F), the remote backup and recovery (RBR-F), the location information maintenance (LIM-F), the delay sensitive deployment (DSD-F), and the network service management (NSM-F). These functions interact with SG-FG, RAC-FG and GM-FG.
8.2.1 Reference points between GM-FG and ECM-FG

There are five reference points acting as the interactions between GM and ECM. GM-ECM-RP1 Reference point between ADM-F and SAM-F. CSC's application service connection information such as network IP and application service transmission status information are delivered from ADM-F through this reference point. GM-ECM-RP2 Reference point between SRM-F and RBR-F. Replica information and network connection information in the distributed cloud are delivered from SRM-F through this reference point. GM-ECM-RP3 Reference point between SRM-F and NSM-F. Notifications of network fault recovery information are delivered from SRM-F through this reference point. GM-ECM-RP4 Reference point between RAM-F and RMS-F. Resource allocation information such as load balancing, time delay and resource affinity are delivered from RAM-F through this reference point. GM-ECM-RP5 Reference point between AM-F and NSM-F. Network connection and SLAs information are delivered from AM-F through this reference point.
8.2.2 Reference points between GM-FG and FGs in CC/RC

There are three reference points acting as the interactions between GM and CC/RC. GM-CC/RC-RP1 Reference point between OMM-F and CM-FG. Resource scheduling, deployment, allocation and monitoring information are delivered from OMM-F through this reference point. GM-CC/RC-RP2 Reference point between SMM-F and SO-FG. Application deployment and monitoring information are delivered from SMM-F through this reference point. GM-CC/RC-RP3 Reference point between ADM-F and SC-FG. The connection and network access information of application services are delivered from ADM-F through this reference point.
8.2.3 Reference points between ECM-FG and FGs in EC

There are two reference points acting as the interaction between ECM and EC. ECM-EC-RP1 Reference point between OM-F and RAC-FG. Network control and network resource information are delivered from OM-F through this reference point. ECM-EC-RP2 Reference point between SAM-F and SC-FG. Status and progress information of cloud service image transmission, monitoring information are delivered from SAM-F through this reference point.

The reference points within GM-FG are summarized as follows: GM-RP1 Reference point between ADM-F and RAM-F. CSC's application deployment information and connection information are delivered from ADM-F through this reference point. GM-RP2 Reference point between SRM-F and ADM-F. Network status information, such as network connection status, network fault alarm and backup connections are delivered from SRM-F through this reference point.

The reference points within ECM-FG are summarized as follows: ECM-RP1 Reference point between RSM-F and RBR-F. CSC's software management information, such as software version and software package are delivered from RSM-F through this reference point. ECM-RP2 Reference point between RMS-F and DSD-F. Scheduling resource strategy and CSC's demand information are delivered from RMS-F through this reference point. ECM-RP3 Reference point between SAM-F and LIM-F. Information of cloud service, such as image transmission status and progress, scheduling policy and runtime information are delivered from SAM-F through this reference point.

It is recommended that the security framework for cloud computing described in [b-ITU-T X.1601] be considered for the distributed cloud. [b-ITU-T X.1601] analyses security threats and challenges in the cloud computing environment and describes security capabilities that could mitigate these threats and meet security challenges. It is recommended that the guidelines for the operational security of cloud computing described in [b-ITU-T X.1642] be considered for the distributed cloud. [b-ITU-T X.1642] clarifies the security responsibilities between CSPs and CSCs, and analyses the requirements and categories of security metrics of operational security for cloud computing. It is recommended that the security framework for the Internet of things (IoT) based on the gateway model described in [b-ITU-T X.1361] be considered for ECs in the distributed cloud. In particular, [b-ITU-T X.1361] analyses security threats to the IoT gateway and to the network and describes security capabilities for gateways and the network that address and mitigate these security threats and challenges.

Relationship between distributed cloud functions and functional components of CCRA (This appendix does not form an integral part of this Recommendation.) The distributed cloud is the distribution of cloud capabilities and its functional architecture extending functions into the functional components in CCRA, which are derived from high-level functional requirements in [ITU-T Y.3508] and functional requirements in [ITU-T Y.3526] and [ITU-T Y.3538]. This appendix describes the relationship between the functions for distributed cloud and functional components of CCRA. The mapping between functions for distributed cloud and functional components of CCRA is shown in Figure II.1. Figure II.1 – Mapping between functions for distributed cloud and functional components of CCRA The functions in CC/RC are extended to the service orchestration, connection management and service capabilities functional component of CCRA, and also the functions of GM-FG are extended to the provisioning, monitoring and reporting, service policy management, service level management and platform and virtualization management functional component in Oss. The functions in EC are extended to the service capabilities and resource abstraction and control functional component of CCRA, and also the functions of ECM-FG are extended to the provisioning, monitoring and reporting, service policy management, service automation, platform and virtualization management functional component in Oss. Others functional components for distributed cloud in user layer, some subsets of multilayer functions remain consistent with functional component of CCRA.
